comment: The identifier vocabulary of the integrations runtime (feature integrations, spec section 6). DATA, not code: both ways to get one entry wrong are unrepairable by running again. An entry wrongly marked strong makes a run attach its data to the wrong element it claimed before; one wrongly marked weak, or a canonicalisation that does not converge, makes a run fail to find its own element and duplicate its devices on every run. Every entry carries an accept pattern, which is what makes a bad value visible instead of silently dropped. The pattern is applied to the CANONICAL form, which is why fronius-unique-id's pattern rejecting a dot is what forces fronius-logger-id to be its own entry.

identifiers.description: IEEE MAC address, assigned per interface. The workhorse strong identifier for devices and clients.
Manufacturer serial as printed on the unit.
Cellular equipment identity, fifteen digits. The check digit is deliberately not verified, so a mistyped value surfaces as a diagnostic rather than being reinterpreted.

An address is a lease, not an identity: DHCP reassigns it, a departing device frees it, and two separate networks duplicate it. Recorded and indexed anyway because it is the only overlap two providers often have.

Weak for the same reason as ipv4. Full RFC 4291 canonicalisation is deliberately not attempted, since a weak key resolves nothing and an imperfectly normalised one costs at most a missed overlap in somebody's query; the accept pattern is correspondingly loose.
User-editable and routinely duplicated (raspberrypi, android). Evidence, never identity.
UniFi site UUID. Provider scope is honest for a UUID; global would have been safe too.

Fronius Solar API inverter UniqueID: a value unique only inside one inverter's own API, so provider or global scope would compose one key for two installations' different inverters and advertise an overlap that does not exist. Values as short as 476 come from independent captures rather than from the vendor's document, which is why instance scope is the highest-consequence entry here.

Fronius logging-device UniqueID: a datamanager card, a hybridmanager, or whatever else fronts the Solar API. A separate entry rather than a reuse of fronius-unique-id because the vendor's own example of a logger id is 240.107620 and the inverter type's pattern rejects the dot, so sharing the type would leave every logging device with no identity and a diagnostic nobody reads. The two id spaces are also not documented as disjoint, so one type for both would let a logger and an inverter reporting the same value resolve to one element inside a single instance.

An AUTOSAR element within a NAMED VEHICLE: the vehicle name, then the element's reference path (the slash-separated chain of short-names from the package root). Case is PRESERVED in both parts, which is why this entry needs the trim canonicaliser rather than one of the folding ones: an AUTOSAR short-name is a case-sensitive identifier, so folding could compose one key for two elements the standard allows to differ only by case. THE VEHICLE IS PART OF THE IDENTITY because a reference path is not an identity on its own. The standard makes a path unique WITHIN one system description, and says nothing about uniqueness ACROSS system descriptions: the standardised platform packages are present in essentially every extract by construction, and vendor package trees are commonly organised by domain rather than by vehicle, so two different vehicles routinely use the same path for different elements.  A short-name is unique among its siblings, so a path identifies an element within ONE model; nothing in the standard coordinates package names ACROSS independently authored models, and the standardised packages are common to all of them by construction. The ARXML form is specified by AUTOSAR's ARXML Serialization Rules (AUTOSAR_TPS_ARXMLSerializationRules, R20-11); AUTOSAR itself is summarised at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AUTOSAR. Instance scope does not cover this. It stops one integration INSTANCE from reconciling away another's, which is a different collision from two vehicles arriving under ONE instance, and a fleet in one graph is exactly that. The vehicle name is supplied by the job, cannot contain a slash, and is separated from the path by the path's own leading slash, so the first slash splits the value unambiguously. The 600-character bound is hygiene rather than a platform limit: the composed claim key becomes a property VALUE and nothing truncates it, so the bound exists only to keep one malformed value from carrying an unbounded string into every index that holds the key.
